sections.title: US Immigration, Citizenship, and Education: Contextualizing Policy and Practice
sections.description: Studies of immigrant incorporation have long been critical to our understanding of how immigrants adapt to U.S. society. Their children face a policy landscape characterized by Congressional inaction on federal immigration policy, heightened levels of immigration enforcement, and shrinking rights for non-citizens. This course will focus on how U.S immigration policy shapes experiences of immigrant incorporation. We will pay close attention to the circumstances of young people and their families, including their experiences of exclusion and belonging across social and educational contexts. We will examine how these factors might affect young people’s development, schooling experiences, academic trajectories and aspirations, ethnic identity, family dynamics, civic engagement, and employment. And we will explore the ways in which community institutions and organizations shape these experiences.
